message.content:
Arrange all 5 chips in a random drawing order.

There are 3 red chips and 2 white chips. The process stops when either:
- all white chips have appeared, i.e. at the 2nd white chip, or
- all red chips have appeared, i.e. at the 3rd red chip.

If the very last chip in the full random order is red, then both white chips must have appeared earlier, so the process stops when the last white chip appears. That last drawn chip is white.

If the very last chip in the full random order is white, then all red chips must have appeared earlier, so the process stops when the last red chip appears. That last drawn chip is red.

Thus, the probability that the last chip drawn is white equals the probability that the last chip in the full random order is red:

\[
\frac{\text{number of red chips}}{\text{total number of chips}}=\frac{3}{5}.
\]

The answer is \(\frac{3}{5}\).
